G290104.description: Sitra (Arabic: سترة or سِتْرَة, As-Sitra), also known as Sitrah or Sitra Island (Arabic: جزيرة سترة Jazīrat Sitrah), is an island in Bahrain situated approximately 5 km (3.1 mi) south of the capital, Manama, which is on Bahrain Island.

G290121.description: Sanabis (Arabic: سنابس Sanābis) is a village located in the Kingdom of Bahrain, in the suburbs of the capital city, Manama. It has an estimated current population of 6564, with a land area of roughly 1.2 km² and a population density approximately 5470/km²

G290187.description: Isa Town (Arabic: مدينة عيسى, Madīnat ʿĪsā) is a planned town located in north-central Bahrain, 8 kilometres southwest of the capital Manama. Designed to serve low to middle income households as a social housing project, it is the country's second planned settlement after the oil town of Awali.

G290215.description: Jidhafs is a town situated in Bahrain.

G290247.description: Madinat Hamad or Hamad Town is a primarily commuter city within northern Bahrain. It was a municipality of Bahrain in the central part of the country.

G290269.description: Dar Kulaib (Arabic: دار كليب) is a village situated in the western part of the Kingdom of Bahrain. The village is close to the Bahrain International Circuit, where the Bahrain Grand Prix takes place annually.

G290296.description: Zallaq (Arabic: الزلاق) is a village on the western coast of Bahrain. Zallaq was the home to the Al-Dawasir, Al-Zeabi and Al-Gahtam and Al-Seddiqi tribes in Bahrain together with Budaiya and Hawar Islands.

G290332.description: Muharraq is Bahrain's third-most populous city and served as its capital until 1932 when it was replaced by Manama. The population of Muharraq in 2020 was 263,373.

G290340.description: Manama (Arabic: الْمَنَامَة al-Manāma, Bahrani pronunciation: [elmɐˈnɑːmɐ]) is the capital and largest city of Bahrain, with an approximate population of 743,066 as of 2025 estimate. Long an important trading center in the Persian Gulf, Manama is home to a diverse population.

G290363.description: To be distinguished from Ras al Hadd (رأس الحد), a district with a famous turtle breeding beach in Oman Al Hidd (Arabic: الحد; transliterated: Al-Ḥidd) is a town in Bahrain, located on a sand spit on the southeastern extremity of Muharraq Island. The town, which has a large native Sunni population, is well known for its rich sea crabs as well as its clear blue seas.

G385038.description: Riffa is the second-largest city in the Kingdom of Bahrain in terms of area. The city is divided into three parts: East Riffa, West Riffa and North Riffa.
